name: Topsoil
description: Loose brown, dark-brown, organic soil. Compressible organic silt (≤0.002”) with inclusions of vegetation and roots. Uniformly-graded, compressible organic soil, not suitable for bearing, and not suitable for use within the ground-filling profile. Suitable for agricultural and landscaping use.

name: Beach Sand
description: Loose, off-white, pinkish-white inorganic soil. Predominantly rounded coarse sand grains (0.025” to 0.08” dia.). Occasional coralline debris and conch shells (up to 2’-10” observed). Roots and minor organic contaminants from the surrounding foliage present within the first 1’-6” below grade on average. Uniformly-graded soil lacking the gradation to facilitate adequate compaction. Suitability for reuse within the ground filling profile subject to engineer’s discretion. If the large coralline debris is sieved from the soil, the high-quality sand may have the potential to be sold.

name: Cayman Rock Fill
description: Consolidated, orange-yellow and greyish-white inorganic soil. Predominantly Cobble supported soil (2.5” up to 8” dia.), intermixed with coarse gravel (0.8” up to 2.5” dia.) and coarse sand (0.025” up to 0.08” dia.). Well-graded engineered soil, suitable for reuse within the ground filling profile.

name: Terra Rossa
description: Loose, crimson, reddish brown inorganic soil. Predominantly consisting of inorganic silt grains (≤0.002"). Uniformly-graded compressible material. This soil is not suitable for reuse within the ground-filling profile. Potential to be used for agriculture due to free draining properties.

name: Marl Fill
description: consolidated, off-white, inorganic soil. Predominantly consisting of angular, medium sized gravels (0.24” through to 0.8” dia.).  Secondary constituents of fine sand (0.008” through to 0.024” dia.). Well-graded soil suitable for reuse within the ground-filling profile, not suitable for immediate contact with basement walls due to water retentive properties.

name: Mixed Fill
description: Loose, orange-brown and greyish-white contaminated soil. Predominantly cobble-sized grains (2.5” up to 8” dia.) intermixed with coarse gravel (0.8” up to 2.5” dia.) and coarse sand (0.025” up to 0.08” dia.). High quantity of organic silt (≤0.002”). Contaminated, gap-graded soil lacking the gradation to promote sufficient compaction. Soil not suitable for reuse within the ground filling profile.

name: Peat
description: Loose, dense, spongy, fibrous, dark brown, organic soil. Native peat layer, primarily consisting of fine fibrous organic material (≥0.002") with branches present (up to 2” dia.). Highly compressible soil not suitable for reuse within the ground filling profile and presents a high risk of differential settlement which can lead to significant structural damage.

name: Shot Rock Fill
description: Loose, greyish white, tan, light brown inorganic soil. Predominantly angular boulders (up to 3’-0” length) intermixed with secondary constituents of coarse gravel (0.8” to 2.4” dia. grains). Tertiary constituents of coarse sand (0.025” up to 0.08” dia.). Severely gap-graded fill. Suitability for reuse within the ground filling profile subject to engineer’s discretion due to insufficient compaction capacity.

name: Crusher Run Fill
description: Consolidated, yellow, orangey-yellow inorganic soil. Predominantly medium-sized gravels (0.24” to 0.8” dia. grains). Secondary constituents of coarse sand (0.024” to 0.08” dia. grains). Well-graded engineered fill, suitable for reuse within the ground filling profile.

name: Native Marl
description: Consolidated, off-white, inorganic soil. Predominantly angular, medium sized gravels (0.24” through to 0.8” dia.). Secondary constituents of fine sand (0.008” through to 0.024” dia.). Minor inclusions of inorganic silt (≤0.002”) grains leading to water retentive properties, as well as cohesion and malleability when wet.  Well-graded soil, suitable for reuse within ground-filling profile, not suitable for immediate contact with basement walls due to water retentive properties.

name: Weathered Dolostone
description: Friable cemented exterior of the bedrock, forcibly scraped off with the excavator bucket.

name: Silty Marl
description: Consolidated, off-white, inorganic soil. Predominantly angular, medium sized gravels (0.24” through to 0.8” dia.). Secondary constituents of fine sand (0.008” through to 0.024” dia.). Significant inclusions of inorganic silt (≤0.002”) grains. nodes of silt are disseminated within this layer leading to high water retention and compressibility when wet.  Gap-graded compressible soil,  not suitable for reuse within ground-filling profile and presents a high risk of differential settlement which can lead to significant structural damage ,
